automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: Only public sources published or visibly updated within the last 7 days are eligible; ambiguous, missing, future-dated, and boundary-only dates are excluded.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub weekly release notes say Copilot app and CLI now honor content exclusions, VS Code adds Agent Merge for review feedback, failed checks, and conflicts, multi-root workspaces bring agent sessions to every folder, and chat sessions show which related sessions need attention.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local instruction and handoff practice should treat content exclusions, multi-root workspace scope, merge-readiness agents, and attention-state session hierarchies as boundary evidence for request packaging and delegated agent operation.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: During ingest, route broad product availability upstream and keep local implications around content boundaries, session hierarchy, and merge-review workflow.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Vercel announced that Cursor Cloud Agents can run on Vercel Sandbox through Cursor Self-Hosted Machines APIs, with Cursor managing the agent harness and inference loop while Vercel provides isolated Firecracker microVMs, durable worker/session handling, and short-lived user-scoped credentials.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Terminal and cloud-agent handoffs increasingly separate the agent harness from the execution environment, so local workflow pages should track where durable control planes, sandbox isolation, and credential lifetimes belong.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Check whether terminal-native fleet orchestration should cite sandbox-per-request and short-lived credential patterns as a cloud handoff boundary.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: VibeEval summarizes early-September agent-harness incidents and defenses, including GitSpawn disclosures from September 1-2, Apollo Watcher Live on September 3, AIR Security on September 1, and Vercel moving Cursor Cloud Agents to Firecracker-backed sandboxing on September 3; it frames harness risk around repository config, package installs, and trusted host components that later execute agent-written state.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The orient-inspect step itself can become an execution boundary when ordinary tools such as git read attacker-controlled config, and review gates need evidence from harness controls rather than only generated diffs.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Prefer primary incident sources during ingest where available; keep this source as a secondary synthesis of September harness categories.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Oobeya published a developer guide that classifies AI coding tools from autocomplete through coding agents, and advises teams to evaluate codebase context, agent capabilities, security/data controls, pricing, workflow metrics, outcome metrics, rollout phases, and review burden instead of choosing tools only by generation speed.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This reinforces the local operating-model rule that workflow, context fit, review load, and measurement come before model/tool selection or tier-specific assistant rollout.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: During ingest, avoid turning the page into a product comparison; extract evaluation criteria and adoption workflow implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AAIF explains the 2026-07-28 MCP specification changes as stateless requests, optional versioned extensions, and direct discovery without a session handshake, with client capability metadata carried per request.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Progressive MCP discovery and tool-governance pages should distinguish per-request capability declaration and optional extension support from older session-negotiation assumptions.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Verify against the authoritative MCP specification before ingesting and keep broad protocol background upstream-owned.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar published an opinion piece arguing that production AI agents need first-class, zero-anonymity identity; agents should use short-lived privileges tied to specific human-authorized actions and operate in contained trusted execution environments before touching production infrastructure.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Event-triggered workflows and acceptance gates need identity, action scope, and containment evidence before autonomous operations are allowed to affect production systems.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Use as a practice-oriented identity-control source; confirm any vendor-specific claims if promoted into governance pages.
